final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor added no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim to a more defensible description of the same record. That narrowing is analytically useful, but it does not satisfy the governing compliance predicate. The admissible evidence still shows a 1.2-point miss in a segment named in two pilot commitments, an open legal question about disclosure, and a policy requiring disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general public guidance favoring documentation and monitoring can support a launch-readiness argument, but they do not establish policy compliance on the unresolved disclosure requirement. Because the caveat here is not merely a disclosure about uncertainty but an unsatisfied policy condition, compliant_with_caveats is not warranted on the present record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the legal intake triage limitation was disclosed in launch documentation for the named pilot use cases.
No admissible evidence shows approved pre-launch risk acceptance covering this named-use-case gap.
The open legal ticket means the disclosure predicate remains unresolved on the present record.
The affected segment is named in two law-firm pilot commitments, which fits the policy's materiality trigger for a named launch use case.
Public guidance on model cards and post-deployment monitoring does not satisfy the internal policy requirement to disclose, resolve, or obtain approved risk acceptance before launch.
